primitives.name: Expectation-Based Valuation
primitives.verbatim_quote: It taxonomizes 25+ AV methods into three frameworks: - **Expectation-Based (EB):** V(S_t) = E[N_{O{t,t+Δt}} | S_t] — supervised learning of expected future outcomes; e.g., VAEP (Decroos 2019, CatBoost, goals in next 10 actions), xT (Singh), EPV (Fernández 2021, CNN+DNN on 15-s windows), Yurko et al.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V(S_t)': 'State value, dimensionless', 'N_{O_{t,t+\\Delta t}}': 'Number of outcomes in time window [t, t+Δt], count', 'S_t': 'State at time t, vector of features'}
primitives.assumptions: Supervised learning of expected outcomes; fixed future window Δt; deterministic or probabilistic outcome generation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When outcome distribution is not well-estimated or Δt is misaligned with action impact horizon.

layer2.mapping: EB valuation maps to GSE's EPA estimation via supervised regression of outcome likelihoods against state features.
layer2.telemetry: Prediction accuracy of outcome likelihoods via log-loss or AUC.

primitives.name: Markov Decision Process Valuation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **MDP:** known dynamics from empirical frequencies, values via Bellman DP (Singh; Routley 2015; Schulte 2017; Van Roy 2021 — Bayesian transitions; Cervone 2016 as stochastic process).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V(S_t)': 'State value, dimensionless', 'R(S_{t+\\tau}, A^{\\pi}_{t+\\tau})': 'Reward at time τ, scalar', '\\gamma': 'Discount factor, dimensionless', '\\pi': 'Policy function, mapping states to actions'}
primitives.assumptions: Known transition probabilities; finite state space; discounted reward structure; stationary dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When transition dynamics are unknown or non-stationary; when state space is too large for exact DP.

layer2.mapping: MDP valuation underpins GSE’s state-transition modeling for situational value propagation.
layer2.telemetry: Convergence of Bellman iteration; policy stability over episodes.

primitives.name: Reinforcement Learning Valuation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **RL:** unknown dynamics learned via TD/SARSA (Liu & Schulte 2018; Liu 2020; Ding 2022; Nakahara 2023), λ-return (Dick 2021), distributional TD (Liu 2022), actor-critic (Yanai 2022), policy gradient (Rahimian 2024), IRL (Luo 2020).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V(s)': 'Value of state s, dimensionless', 'r': 'Immediate reward, scalar', "s'": 'Next state, vector', '\\alpha': 'Learning rate, dimensionless', '\\gamma': 'Discount factor, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Unknown environment dynamics; sequential interaction with environment; episodic or continuing task.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When exploration is insufficient or reward shaping is inadequate; when convergence is slow or unstable.

layer2.mapping: RL valuation enables GSE to learn action values through simulated or real-world feedback loops.
layer2.telemetry: TD error convergence; policy improvement over iterations.

primitives.name: Off-Ball Action Valuation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Off-ball valuation approaches: Wu & Swartz 2023 (actual vs expected defender velocity), Dick 2021 (state value of performed vs predicted trajectory), Nakahara 2023 (independent multi-agent RL distributing rewards across simultaneous actions).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V(A_{\\text{off}})': 'Value of off-ball action, dimensionless', 'S_t': 'State at time t, vector of features', 'A_{\\text{off}}': 'Off-ball action, discrete or continuous', 'V(S_{t+1})': 'Value of next state, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Off-ball actions influence state transitions; simultaneous actions are modeled independently or jointly.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When off-ball actions are not tracked or when interdependencies among actions are ignored.

layer2.mapping: Off-ball valuation extends GSE's EPA to include non-on-ball contributions via multi-agent or trajectory-based modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation of off-ball action scores with actual team performance metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core of action valuation lies in decomposing action value as V(A_t) = V(S_{t+1}) - V(S_t), linking instantaneous action to state change. Expectation-Based (EB) methods estimate V(S_t) via supervised learning of future outcomes, assuming fixed time horizons and deterministic or probabilistic outcome generation. MDP methods compute V(S_t) via Bellman equations under known transition dynamics, enabling optimal policy derivation. Reinforcement Learning (RL) learns V(S_t) through trial-and-error interaction, adapting to unknown environments. Off-ball valuation extends these frameworks to account for non-on-ball actions, which are often ignored in traditional AV. Each framework has distinct assumptions: EB assumes outcome predictability, MDP assumes known dynamics, and RL assumes unknown but learnable dynamics. Failure modes include poor generalization in EB due to limited training data, instability in RL due to delayed rewards, and incorrect modeling of state transitions in MDP. These primitives form a layered architecture for GSE’s EPA pipeline, where EB provides baseline estimates, MDP offers structured reasoning, and RL supports adaptive learning.
